Redevelopment sites

Multi-unit and apartment demolition, taken down in a planned sequence

Demolition of multi dwelling buildings for redevelopment: walk up flats, unit blocks, townhouse rows and the outbuildings around them. More structure, more services, more neighbours and more paperwork than a house, and all four change how the job is sequenced. Send the address and the number of units, and we will quote the knockdown and the cartage together.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Hazardous materials survey across every unit

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    Every dwelling, not a sample of one. Units renovated at different times contain different materials behind the same facade.

  2. 02

    Vacant possession and disconnection of every service

    Who You, with each authority and each tenancy

    Every unit has its own meters. All of them have to be disconnected, and that is the longest lead time on the job.

  3. 03

    Demolition approval and any conditions

    Who You or your certifier

    Multi dwelling demolition usually carries conditions on hours, traffic and dust that a house does not.

  4. 04

    Dilapidation report on adjoining properties

    Who You, through a consultant

    Worth doing before rather than arguing about after, particularly where the block adjoins another building.

  5. 05

    Traffic management and street occupancy

    Who Max, with council

    Where trucks have to stand on the street, or where a crane or a hoarding takes footpath space.

  6. 06

    SafeWork notification

    Who Max

    Lodged where the work requires it, with the notice period the regulation sets.

The detail

What changes on a multi dwelling job

  • Every unit is its own survey. Flats renovated in different decades hold different materials. A sample from one is not a result for the block.
  • Every unit is its own disconnection. Separate meters mean separate authority bookings, and the job cannot start until the last one is done.
  • Height changes the method. Above a certain height the structure comes down floor by floor with the material dropped internally rather than reached from outside.
  • The neighbours are closer. On a redevelopment block the adjoining building is often within metres, which decides where the machine can sit and how the walls come down.
  • The waste stream is bigger and more mixed. Fit out, carpet, insulation and plasterboard from many dwellings, which is why separation on site pays for itself here more than anywhere.
  • The programme is staged. Soft strip, hazardous material, then structure, usually with the site handed over in sections rather than all at once.

What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Asbestos across a whole block is a programme, not a task

Every dwelling is surveyed and the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists under independent clearance. On a block of flats this is usually the longest item before the machine arrives.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

How long does a block of units take?
The machine work is usually measured in weeks rather than days, but that is rarely what sets the date. Disconnecting every unit and clearing the asbestos across every dwelling is what decides when we can start, and both are measured in weeks of their own.
Do you need the building empty?
Yes. Vacant possession of every unit, with every service disconnected. A partly occupied block cannot be demolished and cannot be surveyed properly either.
What about the basement?
That is a scope decision. Breaking out a basement slab and lift pit is a lot of machine time and a lot of cartage, and some redevelopments reuse the void. Tell us what the new design does with it and we will price it that way.
How close can you work to the building next door?
Closer than most people expect, but the method changes. Hand demolition, smaller machines and protection of the adjoining wall all come into it, and a dilapidation report before we start protects both sides.
Can the site be handed over in stages?
Often, yes, and on a staged development that is worth planning for. It has to be designed into the sequence rather than asked for halfway through.

Send the address and the number of dwellings

The address, how many units, roughly when they were built and whether there is a basement tells us most of what decides the programme. We will come and look before quoting.
